name: Detroit
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Detroit: auto supplier diligence, cross-border trade risk, property research and Wayne County litigation.
hero_lede: Detroit is the centre of the American automotive industry and a principal US-Canada trade crossing. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, from supplier and counterparty diligence to property and asset research, coordinating Michigan-licensed investigators and counsel where local work is required.
intro: Detroit is the county seat of Wayne County and the core of a metropolitan area of more than 4.4 million people, with a regional economy of about 331 billion US dollars in 2023. General Motors, Ford and Stellantis North America all have their headquarters in Metro Detroit, supported by a dense network of parts suppliers, engineering centres and logistics firms, and increasingly by electric vehicle and battery investment. The Detroit-Windsor crossing is the second-busiest international crossing in North America, and Detroit Metropolitan Airport is a major hub. After the largest municipal Chapter 9 bankruptcy in US history in 2013, the city has grown for three straight years, reaching about 649,000 residents in the Census Bureau's latest estimate.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Detroit because the automotive supply chain concentrates value, credit and risk there. A tier-two supplier may be thinly capitalised or controlled by undisclosed parties; a distressed manufacturer may move assets between affiliates; a cross-border logistics partner may carry customs, sanctions or forced-labour exposure in its own supply chain. The city's revival has also brought large real estate investment alongside a long history of tax foreclosure and speculative ownership, so lenders and buyers need to know who controls properties and portfolios. Michigan's own licensing rules and Wayne County's court system shape how that work is done.

matters.title: Automotive supplier due diligence
matters.text: Original equipment manufacturers, private equity buyers and lenders depend on suppliers whose ownership and finances may be opaque. We examine corporate filings, liens, litigation, regulatory and recall-related records and related-party links to show who controls a supplier and whether it can perform.

matters.title: Distressed manufacturer asset research
matters.text: When a Detroit-area manufacturer fails, creditors need to know where equipment, receivables and real estate went. We map affiliates, UCC filings, property transfers and successor businesses so counsel can assess fraudulent transfer claims, guarantees and enforcement options under Michigan and federal law.

matters.title: Cross-border trade counterparties
matters.text: Companies moving goods across the Detroit-Windsor corridor face customs, export control and sanctions exposure through carriers, brokers and distributors. We review ownership, directors, enforcement history and trade links in the US and Canada to identify counterparties that warrant enhanced scrutiny.

matters.title: Property ownership and portfolios
matters.text: Detroit property often passes through limited liability companies, tax foreclosure auctions and land bank programmes. We work from Wayne County records, entity filings, code enforcement and litigation to identify the people behind portfolios and assess their history before lending, acquisition or litigation.

matters.title: Wayne County litigation support
matters.text: Commercial disputes in the Third Circuit Court and the Eastern District of Michigan often depend on facts outside the produced record. We support counsel with witness backgrounds, corporate histories and asset research, scoped to Michigan court rules and protective orders in the case.

local_context.title: Third Circuit Court and business docket
local_context.text: The Third Judicial Circuit Court of Michigan, sitting in downtown Detroit, is the general trial court for Wayne County and one of the busiest in the state. Michigan law requires larger circuit courts to maintain specialised business dockets for commercial disputes between businesses, and Wayne County hears many supplier, contract and shareholder cases on its docket. Federal commercial and fraud cases are heard by the US District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan in Detroit.

local_context.title: Michigan investigator licensing
local_context.text: Michigan licenses professional investigators under the Professional Investigator Licensure Act, Act 285 of 1965, administered by the Corporations, Securities and Commercial Licensing Bureau of the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs. Any business offering investigative services in Michigan must have a qualifying manager who meets age, citizenship, experience or education, background and bonding requirements. TDSC does not hold a Michigan licence and uses Michigan-licensed investigators for any local work.

local_context.title: Cross-border legal environment
local_context.text: Detroit matters frequently involve Ontario counterparties, evidence and assets across the river in Windsor. Canadian corporate, privacy and court records follow different rules, and gathering evidence for US proceedings in Canada may require letters of request or Canadian counsel. We plan cross-border matters with counsel in both jurisdictions rather than treating the corridor as one market. Ontario records are accessed through Canadian sources and professionals.

local_context.title: Records and registries
local_context.text: Business entities are registered with the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, whose public records show entity status, resident agent and annual report information. Real property documents for Detroit are recorded at the Wayne County Register of Deeds, while tax foreclosure and land bank activity create additional public records. Personal and secured-transaction filings with the state help trace equipment and receivables in manufacturing matters.

local_context.title: Prosecutors and public integrity
local_context.text: The Wayne County Prosecutor's Office and the US Attorney for the Eastern District of Michigan pursue fraud and public corruption cases in Detroit, including matters arising from municipal contracting and the region's union and automotive sectors. Indictments, plea agreements and court filings in these cases are valuable sources when assessing contractors, officials and business partners. We rely on the public record and do not contact officials outside proper channels.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Detroit and handles matters touching the city from Nashville. We define the purpose with the client and its counsel first, whether a supplier relationship, an acquisition or loan, an insolvency, a cross-border trade review or litigation in Wayne County or federal court. Research draws on Michigan entity and secured-transaction filings, Wayne County property and court records, federal dockets, regulatory and enforcement data, and Canadian public records where Ontario is involved. Field enquiries in Michigan are carried out by investigators licensed under Michigan's Professional Investigator Licensure Act. Reports separate verified facts from inference and identify sources so counsel can use the findings in court or a transaction.

faqs.q: Does an investigator need a Michigan licence to work in Detroit?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Michigan requires businesses offering investigative services to be licensed under the Professional Investigator Licensure Act, with a qualifying manager approved by the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs. TDSC does not hold a Michigan licence; where fieldwork in Detroit is needed, it is carried out by Michigan-licensed investigators.

faqs.q: How do you assess an automotive supplier's financial stability?
faqs.a: For private suppliers we combine entity filings, UCC and tax liens, litigation, customer and recall-related records, property holdings and media to build a picture of leverage, disputes and control. We do not access credit or bank records without a lawful basis. The result highlights warning signs that warrant follow-up through contractual audit rights or the client's own finance team.

faqs.q: Can you trace assets moved by a failing Detroit manufacturer?
faqs.a: Often. Transfers of real estate, equipment security interests and new entities formed by the same principals usually leave a public trail in Michigan and county records. We map these connections so counsel can assess claims against transferees or successors and decide whether to pursue discovery or enforcement.

faqs.q: Where are commercial disputes in Detroit heard?
faqs.a: Business disputes in state court are typically heard in the Third Circuit Court in Detroit, which maintains a specialised business docket. Federal claims go to the Eastern District of Michigan. Counsel chooses the forum; we shape research to the court's discovery and evidence rules. Arbitration clauses may displace both.

faqs.q: Can TDSC cover Windsor and Ontario in the same matter?
faqs.a: Yes, as research coordinated from Nashville. We review Ontario and federal Canadian corporate and court records alongside US sources, and where enquiries on the ground in Canada are needed, we coordinate appropriately licensed Ontario professionals and Canadian counsel. Evidence intended for US proceedings is gathered with both legal systems in mind.
